item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Oct. 4)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Aaron Sorkin on "The Social Reckoning": "Maybe we can't handle the truth"
item.description: Sixteen years after "The Social Network," his Oscar-winning film about Mark Zuckerberg, Aaron Sorkin turns from Facebook's origins to its consequences with "The Social Reckoning," about a Facebook whistleblower.

item.title: Passage: In memoriam
item.description: "Sunday Morning" remembers some of the notable figures who left us this week, including puppeteer Peppino Mazzullo, voice of the mouse puppet Topo Gigio.

item.title: U.S. Marine arrested, accused of killing Japanese woman in Okinawa
item.description: U.S. authorities in Japan acknowledged that a U.S. service member was in police custody and pledged to fully cooperate with the investigation.

item.title: Aaron Sorkin on "The Social Reckoning"
item.description: Aaron Sorkin's Oscar-winning screenplay for "The Social Network" helped define Mark Zuckerberg in the public imagination. Sixteen years later, Sorkin turns from Facebook's origins to its consequences. He wrote and directed "The Social Reckoning," inspired by whistleblower Frances Haugen's leak of thousands of internal documents to Wall Street Journal reporter Jeff Horwitz. Correspondent Jo Ling Kent talks with Sorkin and Haugen about Facebook's power – and what it means for all of us.

item.title: Ken Kesey's original "Furthur" bus on its latest trek
item.description: In 1964 Ken Kesey and his "Merry Pranksters" rode a bus named "Furthur," fueled by music, alcohol and LSD. This icon of the counterculture movement, which has fallen into a rusted state, is now on display in San Francisco, on a journey to restore it to its former glory.

item.title: Ken Kesey's original "Merry Pranksters" bus makes its latest trek
item.description: In 1964 writer Ken Kesey and his band of "Merry Pranksters" rode a 1939 school bus, named "Furthur," across the country, fueled by music, alcohol and LSD. It became an icon of the burgeoning counterculture movement, and a symbol of liberation. But in the decades since it has fallen into a rusted state. Now the bus is on display in San Francisco, part of an ongoing journey to help restore it to its former, magic glory. Jonathan Vigliotti reports.

item.title: Hero passengers on Fly Dubai flight speak
item.description: "Sunday Morning" talked with passengers who heroically helped avert disaster this past Wednesday by subduing the co-pilot attempting to crash their Boeing 737 Max into the Arabian Desert.

item.title: Hero passenger on Fly Dubai flight: "I decided that we are going to survive"
item.description: This past Wednesday, the co-pilot of Fly Dubai's Flight 1073, flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv, attacked the captain and tried to crash the Boeing 737 Max, the jet plunging 14,000 feet in a matter of seconds. Passengers subdued the attacker and another pilot righted the plane with moments to spare. Correspondent Matt Gutman talks with some of the passengers who heroically helped avert disaster.

item.title: Trump announces AI "Super Intelligence Force"
item.description: President Trump announced the formation of a "Super Intelligence Force" after meeting with leaders of the country's largest artificial intelligence companies last week.

item.title: Book excerpt: "Narratives" by Nancy Colier
item.description: In her latest book, the psychotherapist writes about how the stories we tell ourselves about ourselves can hold us back from living a more truthful and connected life.

item.title: Almanac: October 4
item.description: "Sunday Morning" looks back at historical events on this date.

item.title: Letting go: Why holding onto grudges can be damaging
item.description: Studies show people who hold grudges have greater levels of cardiovascular trouble, and higher levels of depression and anxiety. Experts say those taking steps towards forgiveness can have better outcomes.

item.title: Letting go: Why holding onto grudges can be damaging
item.description: Studies have shown that people who hold grudges have greater levels of cardiovascular trouble, and higher levels of depression and anxiety. But according to one survey, four out of five adults harbor some lingering resentment towards others, sometimes over the smallest of reasons. Correspondent Susan Spencer talks with experts about why some people can maintain grudges for years; how holding grudges can be counterproductive; and what it takes to have forgiveness overcome lingering ill will.

item.title: CBS News poll finds Democrats maintain House advantage amid concern about prices
item.description: Here are 10 things to know about the 2026 midterm elections, in no particular order, based on what voters are telling us today.

item.title: Senior Trump administration officials met to discuss Iran war at Camp David
item.description: Vice President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth were among the officials to meet on Friday to discuss a path forward.

item.title: More details emerge about FlyDubai co-pilot who tried to crash plane
item.description: Questions about the motive of the co-pilot who tried to crash a packed flight from Dubai to Israel continue to swirl.

item.title: FlyDubai co-pilot was likely lone wolf, Israeli investigators believe
item.description: The FlyDubai​ alleged attempted hijacking was likely a lone wolf attack, an early investigation by Israel shows, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Supreme Court to weigh energy companies' bid to end climate-change suit
item.description: The Supreme Court will hear arguments Monday over a bid by Exxon Mobil and Suncor Energy to block a lawsuit filed by the city and county of Boulder over the effects of climate change.

item.title: Supreme Court gears up for new term with major cases on climate change, guns
item.description: The Supreme Court kicks off its term Monday with cases involving climate change, President Trump's immigration policies and the Second Amendment among the most high-profile disputes.

item.title: From the archives: Ken Kesey and his Merry Pranksters
item.description: In 1964, writer Ken Kesey, with his "Band of Merry Pranksters," embarked on a legendary cross-country, counter-culture road trip aboard a psychedelic school bus. Nearly three decades later, Kesey (then a farmer in Oregon) rode a replica of his iconic bus along with other Merry Pranksters young and old – with "Sunday Morning" correspondent Bill Geist tagging along – in this story originally broadcast Nov. 18, 1990.

item.title: Latino Dems urge investment in Hinojosa campaign as Texas governor's race tightens
item.description: Latino Democratic leaders are renewing calls for the Democratic Governors Association to invest more heavily in Texas after a new poll showed Gina Hinojosa narrowly leading Republican Gov. Greg Abbott.

item.title: Tennessee prison system head to resign after failed Christa Pike execution
item.description: Christa Pike remains alive but unconscious and intubated after her failed execution on Wednesday, her lawyers said.

item.title: Iowa approves pricy foreign-owned steel plant project in swing district
item.description: President Trump said Monday that the largest steel plant in U.S. history will be built in Iowa. It touched off a week of debate.

item.title: Professor to present findings questioning whether Epstein killed himself
item.description: Michael Freeman plans to publish his research and the New York City Medical Examiner's Epstein autopsy files.

item.title: Newly released footage shows Luigi Mangione's arrest in Pennsylvania
item.description: Body camera video shows Altoona police arresting Luigi Mangione, questioning him about a fake ID and recovering evidence later linked to the fatal shooting of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson.

item.title: Feds charge shop clerk, son with selling illegal kratom after 2 Ole Miss deaths
item.description: Federal authorities investigating the deaths of two University of Mississippi students have charged a store clerk and his son with selling an illegal kratom product.

item.title: American Airlines will let travelers mix cash and miles to pay for flights
item.description: As holiday airfares spike, American Airlines plans to let travelers pay for flights with a mix of cash and loyalty points.

item.title: Amazon vows to invest $1 billion in areas where it builds data centers
item.description: Amazon said it will invest $1 billion over five years to support job education, energy affordability and other priorities in communities where its data centers are located.

item.title: Employers added 29,000 jobs in September, missing economic forecasts
item.description: Unemployment ticked up to 4.2% in September, while employers pulled back on hiring amid economic headwinds.
